sentences.en: Right up there with those fundamental operations is this Adjacent Transform.
sentences.zh: 与那些基本操作同等重要的，就是这个邻近变换。

sentences.en: Let's play a game, folks.
sentences.zh: 各位，我们来玩个游戏吧。

sentences.en: What's the name in the Q language for Adjacent Transform in C++ and MapAdjacent in Haskell?
sentences.zh: 在 C++ 中称为 Adjacent Transform，在 Haskell 中称为 MapAdjacent，在 Q 语言里这个操作叫什么名字？

sentences.en: It's five letters and starts with the letter P.
sentences.zh: 它有五个字母，以字母 P 开头。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 145, recorded on June 21st, 2023.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到 ADSP 播客第 145 期，本期节目于 2023 年 6 月 21 日录制。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we record live from the roads of Italy during the Slovenia 2023 road trip on the way to Venice.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天我的联合主持是布赖斯，我们在 2023 年斯洛文尼亚自驾游前往威尼斯的意大利公路上为您现场录制。

sentences.en: In today's episode, we chat about how to parallelize the algorithm stood unique.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们聊了聊如何对 std::unique 这个算法进行并行化。

sentences.en: Now we can switch to, because we didn't talk about this on the pod, what was it, a couple days ago when we were chatting in the car,
sentences.zh: 现在我们可以切入——因为我们在播客里没聊过这个——那是几天前，我们在车里聊天的时候，

sentences.en: and we were talking about some algorithm stuff, and I asked Bryce, and so now I'll put it to the listener, if you're washing dishes, if you're on a run,
sentences.zh: 我们当时在讨论一些算法方面的东西，我问了布赖斯，所以现在我也把这个问题抛给听众朋友们：如果你正在洗碗，如果你正在跑步，

sentences.en: if you're on a walk, or if you're just sitting on the couch, or sitting in a chair in the backyard enjoying the sunshine.
sentences.zh: 如果你在散步，或者你正坐在沙发上，又或者坐在后院的椅子上享受阳光。

sentences.en: Think about this.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想这个问题。

sentences.en: So we've got the stood unique algorithm, which is an algorithm for removing duplicate values that are next to each other.
sentences.zh: 我们有 std::unique 算法，这是一个用于移除相邻重复值的算法。

sentences.en: And this is similar to an algorithm called deduplicate, or distinct, that we chatted about a little bit.
sentences.zh: 这类似于我们之前简单聊过的一个叫做 deduplicate（去重）或 distinct（求不重复）的算法。

sentences.en: But the difference is, is that one removes all duplicates.
sentences.zh: 但它们的区别在于，后者会移除所有的重复项。

sentences.en: So the easiest way to do this, if you don't care about performance or order, is, you know, in Python, you can just take your list of values and then convert it into a set.
sentences.zh: 所以，最简单的做法——如果你不在乎性能或顺序的话——你知道的，在 Python 中，你只需要把你的值列表转换成一个集合（set）。

sentences.en: And that's a property of a set, is that there's no duplicate values.
sentences.zh: 集合的一个特性就是里面没有重复的值。

sentences.en: So, stood unique, similar to deduplicate, but you're only getting rid of adjacent values.
sentences.zh: 所以，std::unique 类似于 deduplicate，但你只剔除相邻的值。

sentences.en: So the question is, we were talking about the parallel implementation of this in Thrust, but you can sort of think of this, you can sort of think of this sequentially as well.
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，我们之前在讨论它在 Thrust 中的并行实现，但你也可以从顺序执行的角度来思考这个问题。

sentences.en: And the question is, what algorithms, two algorithms are used to implement unique?
sentences.zh: 问题是，实现 unique 用到了什么算法，具体是哪两个算法？

sentences.en: There are two other standard algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 还有另外两个标准算法。

sentences.en: And we'll let you think for a sec while Bryce adds some commentary.
sentences.zh: 我们先让你思考一秒钟，同时布赖斯会补充一些评论。

sentences.en: Because he already knows the answer if he remembers.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他没记错的话，他已经知道答案了。

sentences.en: Well, I don't really remember.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我其实记不太清了。

sentences.en: I do remember talking through this.
sentences.zh: 我确实记得我们讨论过这个。

sentences.en: One of them, I think I said, oh no, it's not remove if, yeah.
sentences.zh: 其中一个，我想我说过，哦不，不是 remove_if，对吧。

sentences.en: It's not remove if.
sentences.zh: 不是 remove_if。

sentences.en: Ah, right, okay, one of them is probably copy if.
sentences.zh: 啊，对了，好的，其中一个可能是 copy_if。

sentences.en: Copy if is correct.
sentences.zh: copy_if 是对的。

sentences.en: Yes, that's the second thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是第二个。

sentences.en: And then, how do you figure out which things you're removing?
sentences.zh: 然后，你怎么找出你要移除哪些东西呢？

sentences.en: Um, a JSON transform, or is it just a JSON difference?
sentences.zh: 呃，是一个相邻变换（adjacent transform），还是仅仅是一个相邻差分（adjacent difference）？

sentences.en: In Thrust, it is a JSON difference.
sentences.zh: 在 Thrust 中，它是一个相邻差分。

sentences.en: And if you actually look at the implementation on GitHub, it actually, it doesn't explicitly mention a JSON difference.
sentences.zh: 如果你去看 GitHub 上的实际实现，其实它并没有显式提及相邻差分。

sentences.en: You see something called, I believe it's called head flags.
sentences.zh: 你会看到一个叫什么的来着，我记得叫做 head flags（头部标志）。

sentences.en: And that is a specialization of a JSON difference where you are using the not equal to, or is it equal to?
sentences.zh: 那是相邻差分的一种特化，你使用的是“不等于”，还是说“等于”？

sentences.en: So it's got, just to clarify, in this implementation in Thrust, it has ON temporary storage?
sentences.zh: 所以它有——为了澄清一下，在 Thrust 的这个实现中，它有 O(N) 的临时存储空间吗？

sentences.en: To, to, to store the, the, the flags that indicate whether or not you're removing a particular element?
sentences.zh: 用来、用来、用来存储那些指示你是否要移除某个特定元素的标志？

sentences.en: Yes, that is correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Um.
sentences.zh: 呃。

sentences.en: And sorry, and, and just to clarify, it's, uh, head, head flags and tail flags are two specializations that just sort of shift where the, the booleans, the truths and falses go.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，为了说清楚，呃，head flags（头部标志）和 tail flags（尾部标志）是两种特化，它们只是稍微改变了布尔值（真和假）存放的位置。

sentences.en: So either sort of, does it go with the first adjacent element or with the second adjacent element?
sentences.zh: 所以，这些布尔值是跟第一个相邻元素放在一起，还是跟第二个相邻元素放在一起？

sentences.en: So that's why they're called head and tail flags.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它们被称为头部标志和尾部标志。

sentences.en: And the flags to indicate where they're the same, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是用来指示它们何时相等的标志。

sentences.en: So, you want to do it adjacent difference with equal to.
sentences.zh: 所以，你想用“等于”来进行相邻差分。

sentences.en: No, not equal to.
sentences.zh: 不，是不等于。

sentences.en: So I was right, actually, initially.
sentences.zh: 所以我一开始其实猜对了。

sentences.en: Because whenever you have a different value, that's when you want to perform a copy.
sentences.zh: 因为每当遇到不同的值时，那就是你想要执行复制的时候。

sentences.en: But whenever they're equal to each other, you want to ignore them.
sentences.zh: 但每当它们彼此相等时，你就会想要忽略它们。

sentences.en: Um, so I, I will again ask the typical question that I, uh, that I, I almost always feel like I ask whenever you ask me.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以，我——我还是要问那个典型的问题，每当你问我的时候，我——我几乎总觉得我都会问这个问题。

sentences.en: Whenever we, we, we talk about how an algorithm is implemented, why can't we do this one pass?
sentences.zh: 每当我们讨论一个算法是如何实现的时，为什么我们不能一遍（one pass）搞定？

sentences.en: Um, and I do admit it's a little bit trickier.
sentences.zh: 呃，我也承认，一遍搞定确实要棘手一些。

sentences.en: To do it one pass.
sentences.zh: 要做到一遍完成。

sentences.en: Um, because doing it, like you could imagine doing it a single pass with some sort of like adjacent view.
sentences.zh: 呃，因为这样做的话，就像你可以想象用某种相邻视图（adjacent view）来单遍完成一样。

sentences.en: Um, but the problem is that it's, you don't just need to see like those two elements.
sentences.zh: 呃，但问题在于，你不仅仅需要看到那两个元素。

sentences.en: Like if there's a run of elements, let's say that you got like, I don't know, 64 elements, all of which have, um, the same value.
sentences.zh: 打个比方，如果有一串连续的元素，比方说你有 64 个元素，它们的值全部都、呃，一样。

sentences.en: Um, when you paralyze that and split it up into multiple different chunks, it's possible.
sentences.zh: 呃，当你并行化它并把它拆分到多个不同的块中时，是有可能的。

sentences.en: That, that, that, you know, one thread could have, um, uh, you know, the, the start of that run of, um, uh, of equal elements.
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道的，一个线程可能会包含、呃，呃，你知道的，那串值相等的元素的、呃，开头部分。

sentences.en: And another thread could have the end of that run of equal elements.
sentences.zh: 而另一个线程可能会包含那串值相等的元素的结尾部分。

sentences.en: Um, and so it's not, it's not simply sufficient to just look at the two elements next to each other.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以，仅仅看紧挨着的两个元素是不够的。

sentences.en: You sort of need some, some information propagated from, um, earlier elements, from, or from neighboring chunks.
sentences.zh: 你需要在某种程度上，将一些信息从早期的元素，或者从相邻的块传播过来。

sentences.en: But I still wonder whether there's a way to do this in a single pass.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然在想，有没有办法用单遍（single pass）来完成这个？

sentences.en: What are your thoughts?
sentences.zh: 你有什么看法？

sentences.en: So it should, we should be, we should be clear here.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们得、我们得在这里把话说清楚。

sentences.en: We're talking about in parallel.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的是并行情况。

sentences.en: Um, sequentially it is very easy to do this in a left to right single pass fashion where you basically just look at two elements at a time.
sentences.zh: 呃，在顺序执行时，要以从左到右的单遍方式来做非常简单，你基本上每次只看两个元素。

sentences.en: And whenever they're not equal to each other, you just perform, uh, a copy.
sentences.zh: 每当它们互不相等时，你就执行、呃，复制。

sentences.en: Um, and you can also do it, uh, in place, definitely, sequentially.
sentences.zh: 呃，而且你绝对也可以在顺序执行时做到就地（in place）处理。

sentences.en: In parallel, though, I don't really see how you can do it.
sentences.zh: 不过在并行情况下，我真的看不出你怎么能做到这一点。

sentences.en: I think it, you, it's necessary to materialize that, that, uh, head flags because...
sentences.zh: 我认为，你、有必要把那个、呃，head flags 显式实例化出来，因为……

sentences.en: I'm not so convinced that it necessarily is, um, this may just be another example of where you need the, um, uh, a reduction that, uh, guarantees ordering.
sentences.zh: 我不太确信这是否绝对必要，呃，这可能只是又一个例子，说明你需要一个、呃、能够保证顺序的归约（reduction）。

sentences.en: A parallel reduction that guarantees ordering, which we've talked about extensively before on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 一个保证顺序的并行归约，我们之前在这个播客里深入讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, you could probably do it, but you're going to end up with, like, a different implementation in that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你大概可以做到，但你最终会搞出一套、呃，完全不同的实现。

sentences.en: If you're chunking things up and doing a unique on each one of the chunks, you would then need to basically do an extra...
sentences.zh: 如果你把数据分块，并在每个块上执行 unique，那么你基本上需要额外去做一个……

sentences.en: So it would kind of be, like, the scan behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以它有点像扫描（scan）的行为。

sentences.en: Not in that you need to keep state.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说你需要保持状态。

sentences.en: Uh, you wouldn't need to.
sentences.zh: 呃，你不需要这样做。

sentences.en: But, like, you would perform, uh, unique on each chunk and then merge that back together, but then still have to perform, uh, unique on that merged chunks result.
sentences.zh: 但是，就像你会对每个块执行 unique，然后把它们合并回一块，但之后仍然必须对那个合并后的块的结果执行一次 unique。

sentences.en: Because if you split a chunk in the midst of a contiguous sequence of equal elements, you're going to end up with two elements in a row, basically.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你在一个连续的相等元素序列中间切开一个块，你基本上最后会得到两个连续的相同元素。

sentences.en: And so you need to remove those.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要把它们移除。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I'm not sure if that, I don't think...
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我不确定这是否、我不认为……

sentences.en: I'm actually, I'm looking at the, the, the, in thrust, the cub special...
sentences.zh: 其实我正在看、看、看，在 Thrust 中，cub 的特化……

sentences.en: Oh, no, no, no, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，不，不，好吧。

sentences.en: I'm looking at, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我在看，对。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: You gotta...
sentences.zh: 你得……

sentences.en: The listener has no idea what you're...
sentences.zh: 听众根本不知道你在……

sentences.en: I, I, I was looking at the, um, the cub...
sentences.zh: 我、我、我刚才在看，呃，cub……

sentences.en: I was looking at the, the, how we implement this in thrust, and, uh, no, Connor is correct.
sentences.zh: 我刚才在看，呃，我们在 Thrust 中是如何实现这个的，然后，呃，不，康纳是对的。

sentences.en: We do seem to do it in two passes right now, which is, I think, unfortunate.
sentences.zh: 我们现在似乎确实是用两遍（two passes）来完成的，我认为这挺不幸的。

sentences.en: Listen, folks, we're headed past a speed camera.
sentences.zh: 听着，各位，我们正开过一个测速摄像头。

sentences.en: I'm happy to report we're not speeding.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地向大家汇报，我们没有超速。

sentences.en: You know why?
sentences.zh: 你知道为什么吗？

sentences.en: That's because the speed limit's 130, baby!
sentences.zh: 那是因为限速是 130，宝贝！

sentences.en: Woo-hoo-hoo!
sentences.zh: 呜呼呼！

sentences.en: We love it.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: We're going 126.
sentences.zh: 我们现在开的时速是 126。

sentences.en: We should, we should clarify that this is in kilometers per hour, not miles per hour for our, uh, American audience.
sentences.zh: 我们应该、我们应该澄清一下，对我们的、呃，美国听众来说，这是指公里每小时，而不是英里每小时。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's the only time, basically, uh, we're not, we're under the speed limit, is when the speed limit is 130, uh, or when we're in a kid's, uh, school zone, because we've got
sentences.zh: 基本上，唯一一次、呃，我们没有超速、我们低于限速的时候，就是限速是 130 的时候，呃，或者当我们处于儿童、呃，学校区域时，因为我们得

sentences.en: to protect the children.
sentences.zh: 保护儿童。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 对的，对的，当然。

sentences.en: Um, uh, what, what is that reduction that we've talked about before?
sentences.zh: 呃，呃，我们以前讨论过的那种归约是什么来着？

sentences.en: Is it a...
sentences.zh: 是一个……

sentences.en: It's a associate of only reduce.
sentences.zh: 这是一个仅限结合律的归约（associate of only reduce）。

sentences.en: Yes, um, uh, so, so a reduce that supports non-commutative operations.
sentences.zh: 对，呃，所以、所以，这是一个支持非交换（non-commutative）操作的归约。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, so this non-commutative reduce, could you do it with that?
sentences.zh: 呃，那么这个非交换归约，你能用它来做吗？

sentences.en: No, this has nothing to do with reductions, right?
sentences.zh: 不，这跟归约完全没关系，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, um...
sentences.zh: 就像……

sentences.en: You can do it in your quote-unquote single pass thing, and I think really more...
sentences.zh: 你可以用你所谓的“单遍”那一套来做，而且我觉得实际上更……

sentences.en: Yeah, you're right, it's not, it's not, it's not really a reduction I need, per se.
sentences.zh: 对，你说得对，它不是、它不是、它真的不是我所需要的某种归约。

sentences.en: More, it's, it's, uh, it's not about really doing this in a single pass.
sentences.zh: 更多情况下，它、它、它不是关于如何用单遍完成这个。

sentences.en: What we're trying to do is not materialize this, uh, flags that looks at the, you know, temporary storage.
sentences.zh: 我们试图做到的是，不要把这个查看、你知道的，临时存储的标志实例化出来。

sentences.en: So I think, I think we should clear it, clean up our, be a little bit more precise about what we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，我觉得我们应该理清头绪，对我们在这里讨论的事情描述得更精确一点。

sentences.en: And you can do that with that strategy of, like, chunking and basically doing, uh, uniques on each of your chunks.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过分块以及基本上在每个块上执行 unique 的那种策略来做到这一点。

sentences.en: But then, like I said, when you merge those back together, you're going to end up still having to do another unique to get rid of the potential duplicate values that are at
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，当你把它们重新合并在一起时，你最终还是得再做一次 unique，以消除那些可能存在于

sentences.en: the edges of the chunks.
sentences.zh: 块边缘的重复值。

sentences.en: Which, like I said, I, I'm not sure if that's going to end up being more performing, because you're basically, you're doing things, I mean, I don't know, a lot of algorithms still
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我、我不确定这最终会不会更高效，因为你基本上是在做事情，我的意思是，我不知道，很多算法仍然

sentences.en: do things, uh, do a lot of extra work.
sentences.zh: 在做很多额外的工作。

sentences.en: So maybe, I wonder if you can do it in a single pass with a scan.
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，不知道能不能用扫描（scan）在单遍中完成它。

sentences.en: I mean, even if you did do it with a scan, that's, that's, and I know you couldn't, you guys are getting rid of stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使你真的用扫描来做，那、那也是，而且我知道你不能，你们在移除东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Uh, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 呃，对，对。

sentences.en: The problem is you need, you need something that can, hmm.
sentences.zh: 问题是，你需要、你需要某种能够，嗯。

sentences.en: And the thing is too, is if you're doing unique on each one of the chunks, you're doing basically like a bunch of copy-ifs, which is going to be super expensive.
sentences.zh: 而且问题还在于，如果你在每个块上都执行 unique，你基本上就像是在做一堆 copy_if，这会非常昂贵。

sentences.en: You're doing copy-ifs on each of the chunks, and then you're doing a copy-if for the final stud unique.
sentences.zh: 你在每个块上都做 copy_if，然后你还要为最后的 std::unique 做一次 copy_if。

sentences.en: I just think probably the implementation that is there right now is the best one.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得现在的实现可能就是最好的一个。

sentences.en: I'm not convinced.
sentences.zh: 对此我可不太信。

sentences.en: Here's the, here, here's a follow-up though, is that, uh, the reason I kind of brought this up was that I love, I love, listen folks, let me tell you what I love.
sentences.zh: 不过接下来还有个事，呃，我之所以提起这个，是因为我喜欢，我喜欢，听着，各位，让我告诉你们我喜欢什么。

sentences.en: I love the fact that there are all these different specializations of adjacent, uh, difference and now adjacent transform.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样一个事实：存在着所有这些不同特化的相邻、呃，差分，以及现在的相邻变换。

sentences.en: I think it's really, like, the fact that adjacent difference has such a bad name is really, it's really, really unfortunate because it is such, I think, an important algorithm.
sentences.zh: 我觉得真的，就像 adjacent_difference 拥有这么一个糟糕的名字，这真的是、真的是太不幸了，因为它真的是一个、我认为非常重要的算法。

sentences.en: It's only, an adjacent difference really is an adjacent transform, but this zip tail type of transform, what's called map adjacent in Haskell and zip with next, I think, in Kotlin,
sentences.zh: 一个相邻差分实际上只是一种相邻变换，但这种 zip tail 类型的变换——在 Haskell 中称为 map_adjacent，在 Kotlin 中我想被称为 zip_with_next——

sentences.en: there's a bunch of different languages that call this different stuff.
sentences.zh: 有一堆不同的语言给它起了不同的名字。

sentences.en: The name of the adjacent transform algorithm is prior.
sentences.zh: 邻接变换算法的名称是prior。

sentences.en: Note that in C++, our adjacent transform argument, our algorithm takes a template argument for the number of adjacent elements you want to look at, whereas prior is fixed to two.
sentences.zh: 注意，在C++中，我们的邻接变换参数、我们的算法接受一个模板参数，用于指定你想要查看的相邻元素的数量，而prior是固定为二的。

sentences.en: There's no way to customize that.
sentences.zh: 没有办法定制这一点。

sentences.en: So it only looks at two elements at a time, similar to how adjacent difference works.
sentences.zh: 所以它一次只看两个元素，这类似于adjacent difference的工作方式。

sentences.en: And in Q, there are actually two specializations of prior because they're so frequently used.
sentences.zh: 在Q语言中，实际上有两个prior的特化版本，因为它们太常用了。

sentences.en: And those are deltas and differ.
sentences.zh: 它们就是deltas和differ。

sentences.en: So deltas is basically prior with subtraction as the default binary operation, but it's commuted subtraction.
sentences.zh: 所以deltas基本上就是以减法作为默认二元操作的prior，但它是交换减法。

sentences.en: So you're similar to how it works in adjacent difference.
sentences.zh: 这类似于它在adjacent difference中的工作方式。

sentences.en: You're subtracting.
sentences.zh: 你在做减法。

sentences.en: If you're looking at sort of two elements at a time and you look at one on the left and one on the right, you're subtracting the one on the left from the one on the right.
sentences.zh: 如果你一次看两个元素，看左边的一个和右边的一个，你就是在右边的元素上减去左边的元素。

sentences.en: So if you have an increasing sequence of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, you'll get back the values 1, 1, 1, 1, 1.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个递增序列1、2、3、4、5，你将得到的值是1、1、1、1、1。

sentences.en: Technically five ones because you copy the first value to be the first value of the output sequence, which I think is broken and we fixed in C++23.
sentences.zh: 严格来说是五个1，因为你要把第一个值复制作为输出序列的第一个值，我觉得这很不合理，我们在C++23中修复了它。

sentences.en: So that's deltas, which is basically the default behavior of adjacent difference if you don't specify a custom binary operation.
sentences.zh: 这就是deltas，如果你不指定自定义的二元操作，它基本上就是adjacent difference的默认行为。

sentences.en: And the second specialization of prior is differ, which is the prior or adjacent difference algorithm with the not equal to binary operation.
sentences.zh: prior的第二个特化版本是differ，它是不等于二元操作的prior或adjacent difference算法。

sentences.en: So it's giving you a mask of basically where elements change.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上给你一个掩码，显示元素发生变化的位置。

sentences.en: And this is a very useful algorithm because there's another function in Q called cut.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常实用的算法，因为Q中还有另一个函数叫做cut。

sentences.en: And when you combine differ with cut, you can basically get that chunking mechanism where it'll split your vector up into sublists and throw it in a table.
sentences.zh: 当你把differ和cut结合起来时，你基本上可以实现这种分块机制，它会把你的向量分割成子列表并扔进一个表中。

sentences.en: We love that, folks.
